title: Perf run 20261019-1119
heading: Frames at rest now redraw only what changed: the opponent's move shows in half the time
meta:
This speed run kept one change, in two commits (71974d8, bb81dc2), plus two fixes from the review (d190b8c, 99b09bb). It is on branch improve/20261019-1119, from base a854807.

While the camera rests, a frame now redraws only the part of the screen where something changed: the piece that moved, the marks that came and went. Everything else stays as the last frame left it. In the final A/B of all 16 primary rows against the base, 6 pairs, the opponent's move appears in 163 ms instead of 319 ms (×0.506, called better). A picked-up piece appears in 127 ms instead of 265 ms (×0.452, better in all 6 pairs, not called). No primary row was called worse. Every frame drawn in part is checked pixel for pixel against the same frame drawn whole, at desktop and phone size.

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the merge. All three items are information the skill asks for; none needs a decision.

items.title: Information: the 1.2× target is met on two rows only
items.body: The change speeds up frames drawn while the camera rests, so it can only reach the moments made of such frames. The opponent's move (×0.506) and the pick (×0.452) pass the target. The player's move (×0.861) does not, because its marks are spread over the tower and one rect around all of them covers most of it. Several smaller rects (ledger DR2) are the next step. The start page, joining, the review and the search are untouched by this change.

items.title: Information: rows more than 3% worse at the median pair, none called
items.body:
The skill lists a primary row here when it is worse in every pair or more than 3% worse at its median pair, called or not. In the final A/B (6 pairs, ab-20261019-1119-final.md):

  • Start page usable, desktop: ×1.273, 4 of 6 pairs worse (0.87 1.37 1.53 1.17 1.51 0.95).
  • Start page usable, phone: ×1.035, 4 of 6 worse. Phone, returning: ×1.060, 5 of 6 worse (one pair 1.89).
  • Start page shows the board, desktop: ×1.070, 4 of 6 worse (0.61 to 1.48).

The start page's own code did not change. The scene's code, which the desktop start page downloads for its live preview, grew by 1.9 KiB (the new damage.ts); the phone shows a picture instead. In step 2 of this run, the same desktop rows leaned ×1.096 and ×1.131 between two commits with no start-page change at all. This lean has shown up in several runs (ledger DL1, FC1). The next general run should measure it with an A/A of identical code.
items.recommend: No decision needed. The next general run re-checks the start page with an A/A.

charts.caption: Start page rows, b353b1b against a854807, 6 pairs (ab-20261019-1119-final.md).

items.title: Information: the change's cost on phones is not measured
items.body: To redraw only part of a frame, the game's canvas must keep its last picture (preserveDrawingBuffer). On the tiled GPUs in phones, that can cost a reload of the picture each frame, also on frames drawn whole, such as while the view turns. Safari has had bugs with this setting. The bench draws in software and cannot see either. Ledger DR8 asks for a look on a real iPhone and Android phone, and for a per-platform switch if either shows a problem.
items.recommend: No decision needed now. If you see stale patches or flicker on a phone after this lands, report it and the switch is a small change.

scoreboard.intro: The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Target: each 1.2× faster than the base a854807 (the dashed line). Each bar is the geometric mean of the pairs; each dot is one pair. Left of 1 is faster.

items.title: Final A/B: all 16 primary rows
items.body: b353b1b (the app as in 99b09bb) against a854807, 6 pairs, 50 minutes: ×1.117 over the 16 rows. The opponent's move is called better; no row is called worse. Of 111 diagnostics, 3 are called better (the opponent's picture handed to the GPU 101 → 34 ms, the longest gap between pictures after a move −27%, draw calls in the player's move 75 → 57.5) and 1 worse: the longest time spent preparing one picture after a move, 7.33 → 14.1 ms. That is the cost of comparing every object with the last frame; ledger DR3, DR6 and DR7 aim to cut it. Memory: the heap +1.1% on a reopened 2,000-ply game, geometries and textures flat.

items.title: The change as Improve measured it: moves and picks, 10 pairs
items.body: bb81dc2 against a854807, moves and picks only, 10 pairs: the opponent's move 271 → 106 ms (×0.394, called better); the player's move ×0.760 and the pick ×0.438, every pair better, not called.

items.title: Step 2: this run's base against the last run's
items.body: a854807 against 3b587b4, 6 pairs: no primary row and no diagnostic called; ×0.953 over 16 rows. The desktop start page leaned slower (board ×1.131, 4 of 6) on code with no start-page change; cold load alone at 8 pairs gave the same lean, uncalled.

rows.change: regression check: a854807 vs 3b587b4 (last run's base)

items.title: The long view
items.body: Not re-measured this run. Run 20261018-1719 measured its head 2.41 times as fast as the first recorded run's base over 13 rows (ab-20261018-1719-vs-first-run.md).

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit, with its evidence in the commit message and the run record.

items.title: A frame at rest redraws only what changed (71974d8)
items.body: Each frame, every object of the tower leaves a signature: its place, its geometry, its material and every value its shader reads. A frame compares each signature with the last frame's. If nothing changed, it draws nothing. Otherwise it clears and draws only inside one screen rectangle that covers the changed objects, where they were and where they are now. The garden behind the tower is already drawn from a saved copy while the camera rests. Any frame that moves the camera, resizes the canvas, changes the garden or plays the entrance is drawn whole. Measured alone, 8 pairs: a picked-up piece appears 221 → 118 ms (×0.524, called better).

items.title: Objects outside the rectangle are left out of the frame (bb81dc2)
items.body: An object that lies wholly outside the rectangle would write no pixel inside it, so the frame skips it and the GPU never reads its vertices. Draw calls in the player's move fell from 75 to 57.5 (called). Alone, against the first commit, 12 pairs, the opponent's move was 12 of 12 pairs better (×0.603) but not called. Together with the first commit it was called: 271 → 106 ms, ×0.394, 10 pairs (ab-20261019-1119-damage-all.md).

items.title: Exactness checked at phone size, and shown to fail when broken (99b09bb)
items.body: e2e/damage.spec.ts plays four moves with full motion and, every display frame, draws the frame in part and then whole and compares every pixel. It now also runs at 390×844 with three device pixels per CSS pixel, and it compares only frames whose garden came from its saved copy, so a frame that retakes the copy cannot fail it by chance. With culling broken on purpose (everything with a known place hidden), 44 of 53 and 50 of 60 frames differ and the test fails; the code as committed passes.

removed.intro: One duplicate removed (d190b8c): the new damage.ts had copied three helpers from backdropCache.tsx (pushAll, pushValue, same), and one copy had already drifted. The garden's signature now uses the tower's helpers. backdropCache.tsx −37 lines, damage.ts +4. The whole run adds about 400 lines of product code (damage.ts, 380) and about 300 of tests.

items.title: Show the game's canvas at once, skipping React's 300 ms hold (RT1)
items.body: From the game's address to its first picture: 623 → 339 ms, better in 12 of 12 pairs, but not called, because the pairs spread by 50% of the mean (the lobby's arrival sets the spread). The computer's first picture −19% and joining −18%, neither called. Reverted; the patch stays in bench/loop/patches/ (ab-20261019-1119-rt1.md).

items.title: Hold the picture of the destination click until the server echoes the move (CH1)
items.body: 10 pairs on top of the kept change: player's move ×0.977, opponent's ×0.959, pick ×0.994, pairs both ways, nothing called. With frames drawn in part, that picture no longer costs a move much. Reverted, no patch (ab-20261019-1119-ch1.md).

choices.intro:
• The change was built as one rectangle around everything that changed, not several. One rectangle is exact by construction; several are the next step (DR2).
  • The two commits were judged as one change, as the ledger planned it. The culling step alone was better in 20 of 20 pairs on the opponent's move over two A/Bs, but never called on its own.
  • Exactness is checked by an e2e that compares a frame drawn in part with the same frame drawn whole, not by screenshots against the base: frames of a moving scene cannot be compared pixel for pixel across two runs. The test forces the whole frame through scene.userData.wholeFrames, read in the shipped render path (DR9 proposes a cleaner hook).
  • The one diagnostic called worse (longest preparing time after a move, +7 ms at its maximum) is accepted as the change's cost, because the moves it serves are faster. It was not re-measured against the commit before the review fixes: those only make the garden's signature also read a texture's version, and the garden has no textures.
  • The start page's desktop lean was not re-measured here; a cold-load A/B takes about 45 minutes and the start page's code did not change.
  • The reviewers' other items were checked against the code and logged as DR5–DR11 for later runs; bb81dc2's missing evidence pointer is in the PR description instead of a rewritten commit.

notConfirmed.intro:
• Frames drawn in part on real phone GPUs, Safari in particular, and the cost of keeping the canvas's picture there (DR8). Only Chromium's software renderer was used.
  • Whether the start page's desktop lean is code or the machine: no A/A this run.
  • The long view against the first recorded run was not re-measured.

next.intro:
1. Speed run: several rectangles per frame (DR2) for the player's move and the pick; the first frame at rest (DR7); a cheaper per-frame signature (DR3, DR6). Then CC2, FM1, QK1, KP1.
  2. General run: stronger guards for the partial frames (DR9: a bound on the redrawn share for a pick and a reply), checks for objects the signature cannot see (DR10), the culled list per canvas (DR11), and an A/A of the start page (DL1, FC1, VR3).
  3. On a real phone: DR8.
